question: Can replacing fixed node activations and linear weights of an MLP with learnable spline activations on edges give more accurate and more interpretable models on small-scale AI + Science tasks?
hypothesis: KANs, built on the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, beat MLPs in accuracy (faster neural scaling, fewer parameters) and interpretability when the target has a smooth compositional structure.
contributions: Generalise the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation to arbitrary width and depth (KAN layers as matrices of learnable 1D B-spline functions)
Approximation theorem (Thm 2.1) giving scaling exponent k+1 independent of input dimension, given a smooth KA representation
Grid extension to refine accuracy without retraining from scratch
Sparsification, pruning and symbolification for interpretability
Experiments: toy functions, 15 special functions, Feynman equations, Poisson PDE, continual learning, knot theory, Anderson localization

method.summary: A KAN stacks layers whose edges each carry a learnable function phi = w_b*silu(x) + w_s*sum_i c_i B_i(x) (B-splines of order k on G intervals); nodes only sum. Models are trained with LBFGS while the spline grid is refined every 200 steps, optionally with L1+entropy sparsity, pruning and symbolic snapping. Compared against MLPs by Pareto frontier of test RMSE against parameter count.
method.task: function fitting / regression, PINN PDE solving, classification (knot signature), symbolic discovery

models.name: KAN
models.params: 15G for [2,5,1] (G = grid intervals); ~200 for [17,1,14] G=3 k=3; O(N^2 L (G+k)) in general
models.architecture: shape [n0,...,nL]; edge function phi = w_b silu(x) + w_s * sum c_i B_i(x); nodes sum; cubic splines k=3 usually
models.init_from: w_s=1, spline ~ 0 (c_i ~ N(0,sigma^2), sigma=0.1), w_b Xavier

other.grid_G_schedule: 3,5,10,20,50,100,200 (toy: up to 1000) increased every 200 LBFGS steps
other.grid_update: grids updated on the fly from input activations

models.name: MLP baseline (sweeps)
models.architecture: fully connected; width 5 or 100 (special functions), width 5 (Feynman); activations Tanh/ReLU/SiLU (Feynman)

models.name: LAN (learnable activation network)
models.architecture: MLP with spline-parametrised learnable activations on nodes; image fit shape [2,128,128,128,128,128,1], G=5

training.objective: prediction loss (RMSE/MSE regression; cross-entropy for signature) + lambda*(mu1*sum L1(Phi_l) + mu2*sum entropy(Phi_l)) in the sparsified runs; PINN loss alpha*loss_i + loss_b with alpha=0.01 for PDE
training.optimizer: LBFGS (Fig 3.1: 1800 steps total, no Adam/LBFGS switching or boosting); Adam for LAN image fitting
training.lr: LAN image fit: 1e-3 for 5000 steps then 1e-4 for 5000 steps; not stated for KAN (LBFGS)
training.batch_size: 4096 (LAN image fit only); not stated otherwise
training.steps: 1800 LBFGS steps in total (200 per grid size, 9 grid sizes) on toy functions; 250 steps shown in PDE plots (read from Fig 3.3)
training.regularisation: L1 + entropy on activation functions, lambda 1e-2 or 1e-3, mu1=mu2=1; pruning threshold theta=1e-2
training.wall_clock: KANs ~10x slower than MLPs at same parameter count (no timings given)
training.seeds: 3 random seeds per hyperparameter combination (special functions, Feynman); seeds 0..99 with lambda in {1e-2,1e-3} = 200 networks (knot unsupervised)

other.best_model_selection: best over seeds and depths, lowest test RMSE or minimal shape with test RMSE<1e-2

inference.samples: 3 seeds per configuration, best reported; no error bars

metrics.name: test RMSE
metrics.definition: root mean squared error on held-out samples, plotted against parameter count (Pareto frontier = fits with no other fit both simpler and more accurate)

metrics.name: L2 and H1 error squared
metrics.definition: PDE solution error in L2 and energy norms

metrics.name: test accuracy
metrics.definition: signature classification accuracy; mobility-edge classification accuracy

eval.protocol: Accuracy compared at equal parameter count (Pareto frontier); 3 seeds, best model reported; no significance tests.

evidence.quote: Both MLPs and KANs are trained with LBFGS for 1800 steps in total.

results.claim: KANs train about 10x slower than MLPs at equal parameter count; authors call it the biggest bottleneck.
results.setup: pykan implementation, not optimised; no hardware or timings reported
results.quote: Currently, the biggest bottleneck of KANs lies in its slow training. KANs are usually 10x slower than MLPs, given the same number of parameters.

results.claim: Signature classification: a [17,1,14] KAN (G=3,k=3) beats DeepMind's 4-layer width-300 MLP with far fewer parameters.
results.setup: Knot dataset, 17 invariants, one-hot signature, cross-entropy; MLP figure is DeepMind's
results.quote: an extremely small [17, 1, 14] KAN is able to achieve 81.6% test accuracy (while Deepmind's 4-layer width-300 MLP achieves 78% test accuracy)

results.claim: An MLP with only 60 parameters reaches 80% on the same task (another lab, unpublished).
results.setup: Knot signature classification; Shi Lab, Georgia Tech; public but unpublished
results.quote: an MLP with only 60 parameters is sufficient to achieve 80% accuracy (public but unpublished results)

results.claim: On 27 Feynman equations KANs and MLPs behave comparably on average.
results.setup: Width-5 KAN and MLP, depth 2-6, G up to 200, LBFGS, 3 seeds, best over seeds and depths; MLP activations Tanh/ReLU/SiLU
results.quote: We find that MLPs and KANs behave comparably on average.

results.claim: The 2-layer width-10 KAN is 100x more accurate and 100x more parameter efficient than a 4-layer width-100 MLP on the Poisson PINN.
results.setup: Poisson equation on [-1,1]^2, n_i=10000, n_b=800, alpha=0.01; ground truth is symbolic, which the authors say may favour KANs
results.quote: A 2-Layer width-10 KAN is 100 times more accurate than a 4-Layer width-100 MLP (10−7 vs 10−5 MSE) and 100 times more parameter efficient (102 vs 104 parameters).
results.note: Superscripts flattened by extraction: 10^-7 vs 10^-5 MSE; 10^2 vs 10^4 parameters.

results.claim: Theory: scaling exponent alpha = k+1 = 4 for cubic splines, independent of dimension given a smooth KA representation.
results.setup: Theorem 2.1; constant C may depend on dimension
results.quote: We choose k = 3 cubic splines so α = 4 which is the largest and best scaling exponent compared to other works.

results.claim: Measured grid scaling is roughly G^-3, short of the G^-4 expected from theory.
results.setup: [2,1,1] KAN on exp(sin(pi x)+y^2); median-based loss gives closer to G^-4
results.quote: a [2,1,1] KAN scales roughly as test RMSE ∝G−3

results.claim: KANs nearly reach N^-4 on five toy functions with known KA shape while MLPs plateau.
results.setup: Five toy functions; KANs given true shape; LBFGS 1800 steps; G in {3,...,1000}
results.quote: KANs can almost saturate the steeper red lines, while MLPs struggle to converge even as fast as the slower black lines and plateau quickly.

results.claim: Interpolation threshold of [2,5,1] KAN predicted G~67, observed G~50.
results.quote: we expect the interpolation threshold to be G = 1000/15 ≈67, which roughly agrees with our experimentally observed value G ∼50

results.claim: KAN parameter count is O(N^2 L (G+k)) versus O(N^2 L) for an MLP; the saving relies on KANs needing much smaller N.
results.setup: depth L, width N, order k, G intervals
results.quote: Then there are in total O(N 2L(G + k)) ∼O(N 2LG) parameters.

results.claim: Special functions: KAN best test RMSE lower than MLP on 15 of 15 (e.g. lpmv m=0).
results.setup: Table 1; MLP width 5 or 100, depth 2-6; KAN width 5 depth 2-6, with/without pruning; 3 seeds
results.quote: KANs' performance is shown to be consistently better than MLPs
results.table: Table 1, row Associated Legendre function (m = 0), columns Best KAN test RMSE 5.25 × 10−5 and MLP test RMSE 1.74 × 10−2
results.note: Exception: iv, 9.28 × 10−3 vs 1.07 × 10−2, is nearly tied.

results.quote: KANs can trade-off between simplicity and accuracy (B, C, D).

results.quote: the bad news is that we have not discovered anything new yet

limits: Scope limited by the authors to small-scale AI + Science problems; no KAN experiment on images, text or large data.
Authors concede mathematical understanding is very limited; no generalised KA theorem for deeper KANs.
Toy scaling experiments give KANs the true shape; the PDE ground truth is symbolic, which the authors say may favour KANs.
Best over 3 seeds and depths with no error bars; compares accuracy against parameter count, not wall-clock; no timings given.
Fast scaling (alpha=4) not reached empirically (G^-3 measured); constant C may depend on dimension.
Unsupervised relation discovery depends on seed; no new discoveries.
Continual-learning result is one toy example.
Training is slow and unoptimised (10x slower than MLPs).
